Findings.Comment: Clamping `last` to `len(lines)+1` makes the subsequent slice go past the end of the file. When a hunk is near EOF and `n > 0`, `ContextAfter` now returns `lines[first:last]` with `last > len(lines)`, which panics instead of returning the available trailing context.
Findings.Headline: Clamp trailing context to the file length — blocking

Expected.why: The clamp sets last to len(lines)+1, so the final slice expression lines[first:last] runs one past the length. With no spare capacity that panics; with spare capacity it silently yields a phantom trailing line, which is the quieter half of the bug.

Findings.Comment: When the requested trailing context reaches or exceeds EOF, this code sets `last` to `len(lines)+1`, and the final `lines[first:last]` slice panics because Go slices may end at `len(lines)` only. A realistic request like `ContextAfter(lines, h, 20)` on a short file will crash instead of returning the available context.

Findings.Headline: Ignore transaction commit errors in AddClaim
